The exported-build run sets and completes all 19 objectives in canonical order in one graphical run.
The rerun battery records 'checkpoints exit=0', and the log reads 'CHECKPOINT REGRESSIONS 12/12 reason=chapter_complete capture_errors=[]'. The first-pass exit-3 contradiction is resolved.
Corrupt snapshots are rejected and checkpoint_reload passes, but no evidence shows Continue being disabled after a corrupt save, or a menu Continue resuming a checkpoint.
Fresh New Game via the real button: objective_set at 20.6 s, objective_completed at 28.8 s, pass true; the screenshot shows 'Objective: submit property'.

Both the exported build and the source build complete a full graphical chapter (reason chapter_complete, 19/19 objectives, 6 mission_complete, 134 shots, end card shown) with no error lines. One recovered autopilot_stuck at (52.8, 0, 0.77) in M04 recurs in every run and should still be looked at.

The spec calls for short dark hair with a grey temple, an eyebrow scar, a grey prison shirt with an orange overshirt, and worn boots. The captures show long slicked-back hair, no grey temple or scar, a single red V-neck sweater, grey jeans and brown dress shoes. Second pass: unchanged in the exe run (D03-032 OPEN).

The spec calls for wavy black cropped hair, a blue prison undershirt, orange trousers and repaired boots. The captures show smooth cap-like close-cropped hair, an added denim jacket and white sneakers; only the trousers and the blue tee match. Second pass: unchanged in the exe run (D03-032 OPEN).

The texture-loading defect is fixed: Adrian's sweater is textured throughout the exe run, including M06 (0129). Hair remains a smooth cap-like shell on Noah (0112), with Adrian's hair a solid slicked mass, so the 'hair not cap-like' criterion still fails.

In the exported build the sweater hem above the trousers is a clean band (0044 zoomed, 0087, 0023), and the cuff in 0101 shows no white triangles. These are stills only; garment deformation in motion was not judged.

The rebuilt GLB still logs bounds of (12.77, 3.24, 7.09) m, above the 11-12 m spec and with an unexplained 7.09 m extent. VISUAL_QUALITY_REPORT claims 12 x 2.5 x 3.1 m, which the log contradicts. Visually the coach reads correctly in iter08.
Panels remain broad flat white. The black wheel-arch trim still renders as detached arcs standing off the body (exe 0006, rear wheel), and the front entry door is a flat inset panel.
Separate wheels with treaded tyres and multi-stud hubs sit correctly in the arches, in both the Blender close-up and Godot. The arch trim defect is logged under BUS-002.
Reflective tinted glazing is now visible (bus_front_true, cabin views) and the side windows have external bars, but the rear window in iter08/bus.png is still unguarded.
Rear red/amber/red lamp clusters and front twin headlamps with indicators are modelled.
Arm-mounted exterior mirrors are present on both sides.
The doors are still static (D03-031 itself says 'doors still static').
Two-by-two seats with headrests, armrests and a leather texture fill the visible interior. These are the baseline seats; only the lighting changed.
The cabin-forward view ends at the new cage partition, and the driver position behind it is not legible in any capture; the front view through the windscreen shows only bars and a seat back.
The glass material is now present, but the paint is still uniform flat white with no wear, and rubber and metal read as plain colours.

CORRECTIONS destination sign, BCF 07 fleet number, a rear 'CORRECTIONS VEHICLE - DO NOT FOLLOW' plate, barred side windows and a steel cage partition behind the driver (bus_cabin_fwd) are all present.
The bus_arrival event (4 wheels) fires and CS01 SH01-SH03 activate; SH01 frames the arrived bus.
Exterior rear, a true front capture (bus_front_true) and two interior views now exist in Godot.
Scanned cracked asphalt with visible aggregate and crack lines reads as a worn outdoor court.
Sidelines, the centre line and circle, keys, free-throw arcs and three-point arcs at both ends are visible and continuous in the close view.
The gooseneck hoop with braced arm, backboard, rim and net is believable. The geometry is the same as the baseline (no Phase 03 change).
The backboard is a plain white slab with a target square: no frame, padding, bolts or wear.
The orange rim and its bracket plate are modelled (unchanged from baseline).
Woven net geometry hangs from the rim (unchanged from baseline).
A square steel post with a diagonal brace goes into the ground.
The chain-link infill now reads at distance in the wide views and in gameplay (exe 0040, P2 viewport). The posts, rails, gate and close-up wire are intact.
Long cracks and patching run across the asphalt (the pattern repeats across the two halves).
Benches, a buttressed perimeter wall with razor wire, a guard tower, floodlight poles and a tap alcove are present. The wall is still tan/yellow (D03-008 open).
In the graphical run both players cross the court and reach the M02 objectives.
M02 triggers fire in order, NPC npc_move/npc_arrived events complete, and guard_attention fires. The floodlight collider retest (D03-005) is covered only by this autopilot run.
Matched before/after images exist with identical camera transforms (cameras.json compared).

Genuine geometry gains: ceiling beams, wainscot, a rebuilt counter with acrylic and monitor, vented lockers and signage. It is still a large empty room with slab benches, a flat box property tray (D03-015) and no security equipment, so it reads as clean and sparse rather than a working intake.
The benches are flat slabs on sticks and the property tray is a plain box; both are prominent in gameplay and cinematics.

Against the baseline, the hall is now enclosed, with a two-tier cell bank, barred fronts, railings, distinct numbering, fittings and a coherent night variant. Scale reads correctly against the characters in 0073/0087. It is clean and sparse, but coherent and believable.
A continuous ceiling with beams and fittings now covers the hall and upper walkways. No sky by day and no black void at night.
Upper-tier walkway railings with posts and mid-rails line both banks.
In-game cells show a bunk, steel toilet/sink and a wall bench (exe 0087, 0073). Basic, but appropriate for a cell.
The upper banks now read A-28 (north) and A-20 (south) and the ground floor A-02/A-12; the duplicate numbering is gone.

The fence is fixed, but the perimeter wall is still tan/yellow (D03-008 OPEN), the backboards are plain slabs (COURT-005), and the yard floor is bare uniform dirt with no court-side equipment, so it still reads as a blocked-out yard.

The washers, presses and lint screen are genuinely rebuilt and believable. The hall is still a mostly empty box with yellow lines, a few primitive grey boxes (bins, cabinet) and little of the clutter a working laundry would have.
The washer-extractors (door, ring, vents, controls) and garment presses (bucks, arms, gauges) are detailed hard-surface models.

The black rectangle on the east wall is gone (iter08 maintenance/maint_brake). The hall has rebuilt pumps, gated route, stair, gantry and pendant pools that read in the M05 wide (exe 0097). Upper areas are dark but read as a dim service space.
The pump sets show a volute, flanges, coupling guard, ribbed motor, valve handwheel and gauge on a baseplate.

Solitary gained a mattress, a fluorescent fixture and wainscot, but it is now evenly bright and clean, so it reads as a holding room rather than segregation. No toilet or sink is in view, and a wall pipe ends mid-wall. The restricted corridor has no matched capture.
Each level has a distinct environment (sky-lit exterior, lit interiors, dark maintenance, night cellblock), and the settings are recorded per capture.
Light pools sit under visible pendants and fluorescent fittings in maintenance, the workshop and solitary.
A directional sun with blue sky casts consistent long shadows from fence posts, hoops and wall.
The self-shadow artefact is fixed and shadows are soft in iter08. Shadow stability (shimmer or flicker) cannot be judged from stills and needs a motion capture.
The M04 chase is now lit by caged amber wall lamps, and both players, the hatch and the HUD are readable in both viewports (exe 0082). Exception: the M04 shim insert (SHOT row).
The daytime yard and the night cellblock/M04 count scenes were captured and reviewed.
Each capture records quality, SSAO, SSIL, volumetric fog, SDFGI (off), tonemap and ambient source. iter07/cameras.json lists only bus and bus_interior even though the folder holds 9 PNGs.
Position, target and FOV of all 10 baseline captures match exactly in iter05 (checked programmatically), and the image pairs match visually.
Five earlier framing failures are fixed, but M03 SH06 now frames empty set dressing with the speaker absent, the M04 shim insert is black, and the M05 handset is unreadable.

The M04 count is fixed (0073). But in M06 SH04 Noah still stands while the guard orders 'On your knees. Both of you' (0127), and in M02 Adrian 'holds Silas's attention' with raised hands facing a blank wall, with Silas not in his view (0040).
One graphical exported-build run plays all 17 cinematics, 36 shots and 133 dialogue lines through to the 'CHAPTER 1 COMPLETE' end card. Autopilot playback only; story feel not judged.
perf_capture now parses. A real-time M01 run (no speed arg, viewports 958x1080 x2 in a 1920x1080 window) records 91.1 fps mean over 13,417 frames. Only M01 was measured.
Frame time is recorded: p50 11.6 ms, p95 13.3, p99 13.6, 0.1 % over 16.7 ms, max spike 142 ms (likely loading).
Static memory p50 215 MB (max 217) and video memory p50 2,476 MB (max 2,627) are recorded.
first_mission_load_ms 6,725 is recorded.
Split-screen performance is recorded at 1920x1080 with two 958x1080 viewports.
Ryzen 7 5700X (16 threads), RTX 2060, D3D12 12_0, quality 2 and window size are recorded in perf_m01.json.
The perf_capture.gd parse error is fixed and the export plus full exe run log no script errors, but no static parse check across all scripts has been reported.
The performance test ran to completion and produced perf_m01.json.
export.log ends with savepack '[ DONE ]' and no error lines, and BreakoutNoWayBack.exe (1.45 GB) is timestamped 00:40, after the last fixes.
exe_chapter.log shows the 'v4.7.2.stable.official' export template (not the Steam editor) running the autopilot to chapter_complete in 315 s, with 134 screenshots, which I sampled (about 40 frames).

The headline claims now match the files (exe and source chapter_complete with 134 shots, regressions all exit 0, perf numbers). Two remain unsupported: VISUAL_QUALITY_REPORT gives the bus as 12 x 2.5 x 3.1 m against logged bounds of 12.77 x 3.24 x 7.09 m, and SESSION_STATE says 'five cinematic reframes' fixed while M03 SH06 regressed.
All four artefacts exist; requirements.json has 646 rows.
Matched before/after sets exist for all ten environment views, plus the bus and the hem texture.

The rewritten report separates geometry, material and lighting changes per area against the iter05/07/08 sets and lists remaining problems. It does not mention the M03 SH06 regression, and its bus dimensions are unsupported (see QA-014).
The script exits 1 unless gate == COMPLETE (line 76), and the current audit reads INCOMPLETE with 511 mandatory rows unverified. Checked by inspection, not executed.
SESSION_STATE (00:47) is consistent with the current evidence files, lists its blockers and points to the next task. It should add the M03 SH06 regression found here.
The launch, regression, chapter, perf and export commands are documented, and the files they reference (perf_m01.json, exe build) now exist with matching results.
